strengths: Uses the #[Scope] attribute for inactiveFor, with a correctly grouped whereNull/orWhere closure so the OR can't leak into other conditions
Uses Laravel 12+ #[Signature]/#[Description] command attributes (verified in vendor) and $this->components->error, and returns self::INVALID for bad input
filter_var with min_range does the validation in one line; --days=0 is accepted and behaves sensibly (my probe confirmed it counts any login before now)
The schedule entry is minimal and proportionate: dailyAt('06:00') plus appendOutputTo a log file
Uses freezeTime, a dataset for invalid input, and a schedule expression test; probes with huge values, whitespace and the 06:00 boundary all behaved correctly

app/Console/Commands/UsersInactiveCount.php:18 — --days=0 is rejected. That's defensible but it's an extra product decision; `$days < 1` could also be expressed with the min_range option of filter_var
strengths: Same idiomatic #[Scope] inactiveFor with grouped OR conditions, and the 'datetime' cast
Uses #[Signature]/#[Description] attributes and a clear, grammatical output line ('Users inactive for 90 days: N')
Tests check both sides of the boundary (exactly 90 days is active, 90 days plus 1 second is inactive)
Also has a dataset covering zero, negative, text and decimal input, a null/datetime cast test, and an exact assertion on the schedule expression and the output path
Uses a typed Event in the schedule lookup closure, and the factory state lastLoginAt is clean; my probes with huge values, whitespace and the boundary all passed

v.rationale: Both implementations are almost identical in structure: a #[Scope] attribute, attribute-based command metadata, filter_var validation, a 'datetime' cast, a factory state, and a Schedule entry in routes/console.php writing to a log. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 13 tests, impl-1: 11). My probes found no real bugs in either. I tried huge --days values, whitespace and '+30', and the exact-boundary case at a fixed time; both handled all of them. The one behavioural difference is --days=0: impl-1 accepts it and gives a sensible count, impl-2 rejects it on purpose. impl-2 ranks first by a narrow margin because its tests are stronger: they check both sides of the boundary, the column cast, and the exact log path in the schedule test. Its output is also grammatical, while impl-1 prints '1 users'. Against that, impl-2 adds a little unneeded ceremony: withoutOverlapping(10) for a single-server, instant query, and an irrelevant Http::preventStrayRequests in the tests. impl-1 is slightly leaner and uses $this->components->error with an INVALID exit code. Its tests are thinner, though, and its output has the pluralisation wart.
